1: # Handoff — premium dark 3D overhaul

12: ## 1. What is being built, and why
13: 
14: `/home/cis/windows/realstate` is a Next.js 16 / React 19 / Tailwind v4 marketing
15: site for **Kautilya Developers**, a real residential builder in Ahmedabad. It
16: was a light "quiet luxury" editorial site. The owner asked for it to become a
17: **premium dark, 3D-first experience**:
18: 
19: 1. A first-visit **onboarding gate**: a 3D human agent greets the visitor with
20:    voice, asks their name; they type it and click through to the site.
21: 2. Models whose **eyes and head follow the mouse pointer**.
22: 3. A scroll-driven **building construction sequence, pillars → finished tower**.
23: 4. A **scrollable 3D apartment interior**.
24: 5. Visual quality is the priority — the owner explicitly deprioritised load
25:    performance.
26: 
27: ### Decisions already made with the owner (do not re-litigate)
28: 
29: | Decision | Choice |
30: |---|---|
31: | Avatar | Ready Player Me GLB (free; ships ARKit + Oculus viseme blendshapes) |
32: | Voice | Pre-recorded ElevenLabs MP3s as static assets |
33: | Building + interior | Procedural Three.js geometry, no sourced GLBs |
34: | Theme scope | Whole site, token-driven |
35: | Gate | **Skippable, shown once per visitor** |
36: | Assets | Build placeholder-first; owner swaps in real GLB + MP3s later |
37: | Aesthetic | "Cinematic gallery" — near-black, one warm gold accent, dramatic single-source light |
38: | Mobile | **Full 3D on phones too** (the old gate excluded everything under 1024px) |
39: 
40: The full original plan is at `/home/cis/.claude/plans/delightful-singing-haven.md`.
41:

44: ## 2. Environment gotchas that will waste your time
45: 
46: - **`next build` and `next dev` can die with `Bus error (core dumped)`.** This
47:   is a **truncated `@next/swc` native binary**, not a code problem. A failed
48:   `npm install` (socket timeout) left it at 13.7 MB when it should be 96.6 MB.
49:   Diagnose with:
50:   `node -e 'require("./node_modules/@next/swc-linux-x64-gnu/next-swc.linux-x64-gnu.node")'`
51:   — a silent `SIGBUS` means it is corrupt. Fix by deleting the two
52:   `node_modules/@next/swc-*` directories and reinstalling. `maplibre-gl` was
53:   truncated the same way (missing its 640 KB `.d.ts`). If anything looks
54:   impossibly broken, suspect a partial install first.
55: - **`npm config set fetch-timeout 600000 fetch-retries 5`** is already set; keep it.
56: - **`pkill -f 'next start'` does not kill the server** — the process is named
57:   `next-server`. Use `pkill -f 'next-server'`. Several confusing "my change

75:   `ref.current`; return the ref and let the caller read `.current`.

77:   object (a `Vector2`, an `InstancedBufferAttribute`) the only sanctioned home
78:   is `useRef`.
79: - **Cannot call `setState` synchronously inside an effect.** Where a value has
80:   to be published from an effect, use a module-scope store read with
81:   `useSyncExternalStore` — the shape `components/providers/reduced-motion-provider.tsx`
82:   already uses. `lenis-provider.tsx` and `lib/visitor-storage.ts` both follow it.

215: ### Design constraints for the gate — these are not negotiable
216: 
217: - **It must render nothing on the server.** Client-only, returns `null` until an
218:   effect confirms first-visit. The server HTML must stay byte-identical so
219:   crawlers never meet a wall. Verify with

221: - **Autoplay is the biggest UX trap.** Browsers block audio without a gesture,
222:   and `CLAUDE.md` §6 independently lists autoplay audio under *Avoid*. The
223:   design: the avatar is visible, breathing, blinking and already tracking the
224:   cursor **in silence**; `audio.play()` is attempted optimistically; on rejection

226:   input and a visible **Skip** are usable throughout. **Captions render the line
227:   as text regardless** — so the silent path is complete, not degraded. Test in
228:   Safari; iOS respects the hardware mute switch even after a valid gesture.

230:   the words with no audio). That is the argument for it over amplitude.
231: - Escape hatches: visible Skip, `Escape` key, `?nogate=1`, and a ~6 s failsafe so
232:   a failed chunk can never permanently occlude the site.

234:   Gate `z-[90]`, skip link `z-[110]`.

273:   MapLibre, Pannellum and Framer Motion were removed. All three are installed
274:   and actively imported — commit `c85c131` restored them and the README was

277:   importers. Delete in Phase 6.

282:   `carpetArea: 0`. Consequently the Money, Specifications and Progress sections
283:   on `/projects/[slug]` **do not render at all**.

287: ## 8. Conventions to match
288: 
289: - **Server Components by default.** `"use client"` only where a hook or listener
290:   demands it. Indexable content must live in server-rendered HTML — most AI
291:   crawlers never execute JS.
292: - **The `deferred-*` convention:** a `"use client"` shim holding one
293:   `dynamic(() => import(...).then(m => m.X), { ssr:false, loading: <height-reserving skeleton> })`
294:   plus a thin prop-forwarding wrapper. Four already exist; copy their shape.
295: - **The two-gate 3D mount** (`components/projects/master-plan.tsx` is canonical):
296:   capability check → IntersectionObserver → `requestIdleCallback` → render inside
297:   `<WebGLBoundary>`.
298: - **Never allocate inside `useFrame`.** Scratch `Vector3`/`Matrix4`/`Quaternion`
299:   at module scope and recycle. `CLAUDE.md` §7 is explicit and
300:   `tower-construction.tsx` follows it strictly.
301: - Framer Motion is used through `<LazyMotion strict>` — import `m`, never
302:   `motion`, or it throws at runtime.
303: - Next 16 specifics: globally-injected `LayoutProps<"/">` / `PageProps<"/x/[y]">`
304:   types (not imported), `await params`, typed routes (a `<Link>` to a
305:   non-existent route fails the build).
306: - **Comment style matters here.** The codebase explains *why*, in a first-person
307:   engineering voice, often citing `CLAUDE.md §n`. Match it; do not strip it.

312:   `"AWAITING CLIENT"` and every project reads the same. RERA §59 attaches
313:   penalties of up to 10% of project cost to the advertisement itself, and a
314:   website is an advertisement.
315: - Every 3D surface needs an **"Artist's impression / indicative, not to scale"**
316:   caption. The procedural tower is not a real Kautilya building and must stay
317:   visibly schematic. §12 makes the promoter liable for misleading visuals and a
318:   disclaimer does not waive that.

320:   project page and in the footer (§11(2)).

333:    meshes `Wolf3D_Head`, `Wolf3D_Teeth`, `EyeLeft`, `EyeRight`. **Apply jaw
334:    morphs to `Wolf3D_Head` *and* `Wolf3D_Teeth`** or the teeth float in place.
335: 2. **Three MP3s** into `public/audio/agent/` matching `lib/agent-script.ts`.
336:    An Indian-English female voice will land far better than a generic American
337:    one. ⚠ **ElevenLabs' free tier generally prohibits commercial use** — this is
338:    a real business site, so it likely needs a paid plan. The owner has been told.
339: 3. **Real RERA registration numbers** when they arrive.

345: ```bash
346: npx tsc --noEmit      # fastest signal
347: npm run lint
348: npm run build         # typed routes; must pass
349: (setsid nohup npx next start --port 3111 > /tmp/start3111.log 2>&1 < /dev/null &)

353:   the `<h1>` present.

355: - Reduced motion (DevTools → Rendering): gate must not appear, 3D falls back.

363: The owner said not to prioritise performance; `CLAUDE.md` §15 demands Lighthouse

368:   reserved dimensions, real fallbacks, server-rendered content behind the canvas.
369: - **Skipped**, because they only buy load time: OffscreenCanvas workers, Draco
370:   compression, KTX2 textures.
371: 
372: Expect mobile Lighthouse performance below 90. That is a decision, not a defect.

121:  * real carpet area. The proportions are schematic; the areas are not.

123: export function roomDimensions(room: Room, carpetAreaSqFt: number): string {
124:   const areaSqM = carpetAreaSqFt * room.share * 0.092903;
125:   // Recover a plausible rectangle from the area using the drawn aspect ratio.
126:   const aspect = room.w / room.h;
127:   const height = Math.sqrt(areaSqM / aspect);
128:   const width = areaSqM / height;
129:   return `${width.toFixed(1)} × ${height.toFixed(1)} m`;

70: ## 3. Lint rules that will reject the obvious code
71: 
72: The React Compiler lint is strict and rejected three separate idioms:
73: 
74: - **Cannot read a ref's `.current` during render.** So a hook cannot return
75:   `ref.current`; return the ref and let the caller read `.current`.
76: - **Cannot mutate a `useState` or `useMemo` value.** For a per-frame mutable
77:   object (a `Vector2`, an `InstancedBufferAttribute`) the only sanctioned home
78:   is `useRef`.
79: - **Cannot call `setState` synchronously inside an effect.** Where a value has
80:   to be published from an effect, use a module-scope store read with
81:   `useSyncExternalStore` — the shape `components/providers/reduced-motion-provider.tsx`
82:   already uses. `lenis-provider.tsx` and `lib/visitor-storage.ts` both follow it.
83: 
84: Always run **`npx tsc --noEmit` and `npm run lint`** before `npm run build`;
85: they are much faster and catch nearly everything.

1: # Ahmedabad builder website
2: 
3: A quiet-luxury marketing site for a mid-to-premium residential developer in
4: Ahmedabad. Multi-project brand site, not a single-project microsite.
5: 
6: The full brief — market research, design system, legal obligations, phased
7: build order — lives in [`CLAUDE.md`](./CLAUDE.md). Read it before changing
8: anything visual or legal.
9: 
10: ## Getting started
11: 
12: ```bash
13: npm install
14: npm run dev     # http://localhost:3000
15: npm run build   # production build
16: npm run lint
17: ```
18: 
19: ## The config file
20: 
21: Everything client-specific lives in **`lib/site-config.ts`** — brand name,
22: phone, WhatsApp number, email, office address, geo coordinates, socials, RERA
23: identity and the festive-offer switch. Nothing else in the codebase hardcodes
24: these. To rebrand the site, edit that one file.
25: 
26: Two fields deserve care:
27: 
28: - `whatsapp` must be **E.164 digits only** (`919999999999`, no `+` or spaces) —
29:   that is what the `wa.me` deep-link format requires.
30: - `rera.promoterNumber` ships as `DEMO-PENDING`. **Never replace it with an
31:   invented number.** RERA Act §59 attaches penalties of up to 10% of estimated
32:   project cost to the advertisement itself, and a website is an advertisement.
33: 
34: Set `NEXT_PUBLIC_SITE_URL` in the environment to control canonical URLs,
35: `metadataBase` and Open Graph URLs. It falls back to `https://example.com`.
36: 
37: ## What exists today
38: 
39: All five build phases from `CLAUDE.md` §16 are implemented.
40: 
41: **Content & data**
42: - `lib/data.ts` is the CMS seam. It reads from `lib/placeholders/` today and every
43:   function is async, returning the shapes a Sanity query would. Wiring the CMS
44:   means rewriting that one file — no component changes.
45: - Six demo projects, six micro-markets, twelve amenities, three testimonials,
46:   three long-form insight posts.
47: 
48: **Pages** — home, projects listing (URL-synced filters), project detail,
49: locations index + six corridor guides, amenities, gallery, about/legacy,
50: NRI corner, insights + three articles, contact, channel partners, careers,
51: RERA disclosure, privacy, terms, 404.
52: 
53: **Tools**
54: - Floor-plan viewer: schematic SVG per configuration, wheel/drag zoom and pan,
55:   keyboard controls (`+`, `-`, `0`, arrows), north compass rotated to the unit's
56:   facing, room dimensions derived from real carpet area.
57: - EMI calculator: reducing-balance amortisation, four live inputs.
58: - Cost sheet: agreement value, GST, Gujarat stamp duty, registration,
59:   maintenance advance — server-rendered so it stays crawlable.
60: - Brochure: ungated download plus an optional name-and-phone gate.
61: - Gallery lightbox: Embla, keyboard-navigable, Escape to close.
62: 
63: **3D** — WebGL hero, clickable master-plan massing, and a 360° panorama, all
64: gated behind `lib/webgl.ts` (real context probe, pointer type, viewport,
65: cores/memory, reduced-motion) and wrapped in `components/webgl-boundary.tsx`.
66: Every one sits over content that already works without it.
67: 
68: **SEO** — sitemap (29 URLs), robots, `/llms.txt` generated from live data,
69: per-project OG images via `next/og`, and JSON-LD throughout:
70: `RealEstateAgent` site-wide, `Apartment`/`SingleFamilyResidence` + `Offer`,
71: `Place`, `Article`, `BreadcrumbList` and `FAQPage`.
72: 
73: ## Measured performance
74: 
75: Production build, Lighthouse mobile, on a developer laptop — **not CI**. Expect
76: ±5 points of run-to-run variance; stop every dev server first, or scores drop
77: by 15.
78: 
79: | Page | Perf | A11y | Best practices | LCP | CLS |
80: |---|---|---|---|---|---|
81: | `/` | 95 | 100 | 100 | 2.9s | 0 |
82: | `/projects` | 98 | 100 | 100 | 2.1s | 0 |
83: | `/projects/[slug]` | 86–90 | 100 | 100 | 3.0s | 0 |
84: | `/locations/[slug]` | 95 | 100 | 100 | 2.9s | 0 |
85: | `/amenities` | 97 | 100 | 100 | 2.6s | 0 |
86: | `/gallery` | 90 | 100 | 100 | 2.8s | 0 |
87: | `/about` | 90 | 100 | 100 | 2.9s | 0 |
88: 
89: Desktop is 100 across performance, accessibility and best practices.
90: Accessibility is 100 on every page measured.
91: 
92: **Open against the §15 targets:**
93: - `/projects/[slug]` straddles the mobile ≥90 gate (86–90 across runs). It is by
94:   far the heaviest page — ~142KB of HTML and eight interactive blocks. Every one
95:   of those blocks is already dynamically imported.
96: - LCP runs 2.1–3.0s against a ≤2.5s target on the heavier pages. The LCP element
97:   is hero body text and the delay is the webfont swap; `size-adjust` fallback
98:   tuning is the next lever.
99: 
100: Lighthouse reports SEO as 0 under Node 20.14 because its `canonical` audit calls
101: `URL.parse` (Node 22+). Every individual SEO audit passes — upgrade Node for a
102: real score.
103: 
104: ## Three deliberate stack deviations
105: 
106: `CLAUDE.md` §4 specifies MapLibre, Pannellum and Framer Motion. None are used,
107: and §4 records why:
108: 
109: - **MapLibre → hand-drawn SVG.** ~200KB gzip and a keyed tile provider, versus
110:   ~3KB, no key and a map that matches the brand.
111: - **Pannellum → Three.js sphere.** Three was already in the bundle; a second
112:   renderer bought nothing.
113: - **Framer Motion → IntersectionObserver + CSS.** This one was measured, not
114:   assumed: a dozen `motion.div` instances per page cost 150–300ms of blocking
115:   time. Removing it moved amenities from 74 to 97 and the project page from 65
116:   to 88.
117: 
118: ## Conventions
119: 
120: - Server Components by default. `"use client"` only where a hook or listener
121:   demands it — indexable content must stay in the server-rendered HTML,
122:   because most AI crawlers never execute JS.
123: - Animate `opacity` and `transform` only, and stay under 500ms.
124: - Never merge `.eyebrow` with a `text-*` colour through `cn()` without checking
125:   the result: tailwind-merge treats same-prefix classes as conflicting. That
126:   collision is why the class is not called `.text-luxury`.

## Measured performance

Production build, Lighthouse mobile, on a developer laptop — **not CI**. Expect
±5 points of run-to-run variance; stop every dev server first, or scores drop
by 15.

| Page | Perf | A11y | Best practices | LCP | CLS |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| `/` | 95 | 100 | 100 | 2.9s | 0 |
| `/projects` | 98 | 100 | 100 | 2.1s | 0 |
| `/projects/[slug]` | 86–90 | 100 | 100 | 3.0s | 0 |
| `/locations/[slug]` | 95 | 100 | 100 | 2.9s | 0 |
| `/amenities` | 97 | 100 | 100 | 2.6s | 0 |
| `/gallery` | 90 | 100 | 100 | 2.8s | 0 |
| `/about` | 90 | 100 | 100 | 2.9s | 0 |

Desktop is 100 across performance, accessibility and best practices.
Accessibility is 100 on every page measured.

**Open against the §15 targets:**
- `/projects/[slug]` straddles the mobile ≥90 gate (86–90 across runs). It is by
  far the heaviest page — ~142KB of HTML and eight interactive blocks. Every one
  of those blocks is already dynamically imported.
- LCP runs 2.1–3.0s against a ≤2.5s target on the heavier pages. The LCP element
  is hero body text and the delay is the webfont swap; `size-adjust` fallback
  tuning is the next lever.

Lighthouse reports SEO as 0 under Node 20.14 because its `canonical` audit calls
`URL.parse` (Node 22+). Every individual SEO audit passes — upgrade Node for a
real score.

## Three deliberate stack deviations

`CLAUDE.md` §4 specifies MapLibre, Pannellum and Framer Motion. None are used,
and §4 records why:

- **MapLibre → hand-drawn SVG.** ~200KB gzip and a keyed tile provider, versus
  ~3KB, no key and a map that matches the brand.
- **Pannellum → Three.js sphere.** Three was already in the bundle; a second
  renderer bought nothing.
- **Framer Motion → IntersectionObserver + CSS.** This one was measured, not
  assumed: a dozen `motion.div` instances per page cost 150–300ms of blocking
  time. Removing it moved amenities from 74 to 97 and the project page from 65
  to 88.
